semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Brachytherapy is a direct subset of brachytherapy dosimetry which focuses on the measurement and calculation of doses delivered through brachytherapy. Thus, while not entirely semantically equivalent, it is the closest match available in this list.

parent_domains.justification: Brachytherapy dosimetry is a part of the broader brachytherapy field, focusing on the dosimetric calculations and measurements.
Brachytherapy is a type of radiation therapy, thus making radiation therapy a broader category encompassing brachytherapy dosimetry.
Radiation oncology covers all types of radiation treatments for cancer, including brachytherapy and its dosimetry.
Oncology is the study and treatment of tumors and cancer, under which treatments like brachytherapy fall.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Given the specificity of brachytherapy dosimetry, brachytherapy is the closest parent as it is specifically focused on this mode of treatment.

child_domains.justification: Intravascular brachytherapy is a specialized form of brachytherapy, which implies specific dosimetry considerations thus can be a child under brachytherapy dosimetry.

closest_child_domain.justification: Intravascular brachytherapy is the closest child domain as it is directly a specialized application within the broader category of brachytherapy treatments, which requires specific dosimetric calculations.

sibling_domains.justification: Treatment planning is an essential part of the brachytherapy process and is closely related to dosimetry as it involves planning the dose distributions for treatment.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: This domain is the closest sibling to brachytherapy dosimetry as it directly involves calculating and planning the dosages, which is fundamentally linked to dosimetry.

unrelated_domains.justification: Nuclear medicine involves the use of radioactive substances to diagnose or treat diseases but is distinct from brachytherapy dosimetry.
This domain focuses on statistical treatment effect estimates, which is unrelated to the physical and technical aspects of brachytherapy dosimetry.
Radiology involves imaging techniques rather than the therapeutic dose calculations central to dosimetry.
Cardiology is concerned with heart-related conditions, having no direct link to brachytherapy dosimetry.
Though related to targeted radiation therapies, this domain is more distinct from dosimetry related to brachytherapy.
Precision medicine is a broader approach defining individual treatment plans, not specifically focusing on radiation dose calculations like dosimetry.
Oncology imaging focuses on the visualization of cancer, which is distinct from dose calculation processes like dosimetry.
